verses.1: And Azariah, son of Oded, was covered with the spirit of God.
verses.2: And he went before Assuero, and said to him, “Listen to me, Assuero, and all of Judah. The LORD will be with you during your time here. If you ask for help from Him, He will surely provide for you. But if you turn away from Him, He will also leave you.”
verses.3: And many days will pass for Israel, without the true God, without a prophet who can guide them, and without a Torah.
verses.4: And he sat down in his misery before Jehovah, the God of Israel. He sought Him, and he found Him.
verses.5: And in those times, there is no peace for those who go out or come in, because there are many deaths among all the inhabitants of the earth.
verses.6: And nations were divided among themselves, and cities were destroyed in each other’s midst. But God remained present everywhere.
verses.7: And you shall be strong, and your hands shall not be weakened, for there is reward for your efforts.
verses.8: And when Asa heard these words and the prophecies, the prophet became even more determined. He sent out his followers from all over Judah and Benjamin, as well as from the cities near Ephraim. They rebuilt the Temple of Yahweh, which had been destroyed before.
verses.9: And he gathered together all of Judah, along with the Benjamites and the foreigners with them, from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Shimon. They fell upon him because they thought that Jehovah, their God, was with him.
verses.10: And Jerusalem was captured on the third month, in the fifteenth year of Ahas’s reign.
verses.11: And they offered sacrifices to Jehovah on that day. They brought seven thousand sheep and seven thousand lambs.
verses.12: And they came into covenant with Jehovah, their God, with all their hearts and with all their souls.
verses.13: And everyone who does not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, will die from childhood until old age, both men and women.
verses.14: And they rejoiced in the LORD with a loud cry and with shouting, and with trumpets and drums.
verses.15: And all of Israel rejoiced over this victory, for in their hearts they praised God. They also prayed to Him earnestly. And God answered their prayers and delivered them from all their troubles.
verses.16: And also, when Asa became king, he removed the idol from Gibeah that she had made for Asherah. Asa destroyed that idol and burned it in the river Kedron.
verses.17: And the idols did not leave Israel. Only the heart of Assyria was whole throughout all its days.
verses.18: And he brought the sacred objects of his father’s house into the Temple of God: gold, silver, and all kinds of treasures.
verses.19: And there was no war until the age of thirty-five during Ahasuerus’ reign.
